definitions.explanation: The historical period of Emperor Meiji's reign, 1868–1912, when Japan rapidly modernized and Westernized after the end of the feudal Edo period.

examples.japanese: {明治|めいじ}{時代|じだい}に{生|う}まれた{作家|さっか}。
examples.english: a writer born in the Meiji period.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}は{明治|めいじ}{時代|じだい}に{大|おお}きく{近代化|きんだいか}した。
examples.english: Japan modernized greatly during the Meiji period.

examples.japanese: {明治|めいじ}{時代|じだい}には、{西洋|せいよう}の{文化|ぶんか}や{技術|ぎじゅつ}が{次々|つぎつぎ}と{取|と}り{入|い}れられた。
examples.english: During the Meiji period, Western culture and technology were adopted one after another.

notes:
Compound of {明治|めいじ} (the era name) + {時代|じだい} (period, era). Refers to 1868–1912, when Japan transformed from a feudal society into a modern industrial nation-state.

KEY ASSOCIATIONS:
- {明治維新|めいじいしん}: the Meiji Restoration (1868)
- {文明開化|ぶんめいかいか}: the 'civilization and enlightenment' of rapid Westernization

RELATED PERIODS:
- {江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}: Edo period — the preceding feudal era
- {大正|たいしょう}{時代|じだい}: Taisho period — the era that followed (1912–1926)
